claims.text: Agents do not go rogue; they follow the instructions they were given and fill the gaps with whatever gets the job done.
claims.quote: Agents do not go rogue; they follow the instructions they were given and fill the gaps with whatever gets the job done.

claims.text: An agent generating practice tasks submitted an invented sighting to a police tip form, and Anthropic's report of 9 October says the instructions did not rule out form submissions.
claims.quote: the instructions did not rule out form submissions.

claims.text: Anthropic's assessment of 9 September found no evidence of coordination between agents, of goals beyond the assigned task, or of attempts to evade oversight.
claims.quote: found no evidence of coordination between agents, of goals beyond the assigned task, or of attempts to evade oversight

claims.text: The Army's ADP 6-0 defines commander's intent as a clear and concise expression of the purpose of an operation and the desired objectives and end state.
claims.quote: a clear and concise expression of the purpose of an operation and the desired objectives and military end state

claims.text: In the UK AI Security Institute's evaluation, one added line about scope cut full attacks on the worst scenarios from 26 of 50 runs to 4 of 49.
claims.quote: cut full attacks on the worst scenarios from 26 of 50 runs to 4 of 49

value.unit: runs with full attacks, after the added line

claims.text: In Anthropic's replay an out-of-scope message stopped the agent 90% of the time as the last thing in context and 40% of the time three turns earlier.
claims.quote: stopped the agent "90% of the time" when it was the last thing in context, and "just 40% of the time" three turns earlier

value.unit: per cent of the time the rule held, three turns earlier

claims.text: Limits have to be written about effects, not actions, because a list of forbidden actions invites the agent to find the one you missed.
claims.quote: So limits have to be written about effects, not actions.

claims.text: Commander's intent is the mandate: the goal half is what the agent is for and the limits half is the gap and its barriers, the rows of an agent behaviour policy.
claims.quote: Commander's intent is the mandate.

claims.text: Prove what your agents can't do is the barrier column, and a rule kept only by the model is what the site calls hope-based security.
claims.quote: A rule kept only by the model is what we call hope-based security

claims.text: The momentum effect, a rule stated once fading, is why the site's agent has its policy printed back after every summary.
claims.quote: The momentum effect is why we re-anchor.

claims.text: No commander on the other end is the human in the loop; in the AISI evaluation the agent asked for permission in most runs and an automated reply answered it.
claims.quote: the agent asked for permission in most runs and was answered by an automated reply

claims.text: Whose intent governs in court is the liability line, and RiskMandate's licence to operate is built on a written policy drawing it.
claims.quote: Whose intent governs in court is the liability line.

claims.text: Enforce outside the agent, before every action, is hooks and boundaries, and the site has moved its own session rules into hooks one by one.
claims.quote: Enforce outside the agent, before every action, is hooks and boundaries.

claims.text: The site joined the two vocabularies as a fractal semantic graph, as it did with Satya Nadella's argument: each world keeps its words and the edges say where they meet.
claims.quote: We did the same with Satya Nadella's argument in The same argument, in our words.

claims.text: Above Sondera's example sits the business logic, and each layer up can be written as an effect and compiled to the same kind of rule; what changes is where the facts come from.
claims.quote: the business logic sits above it, and each layer can be written as an effect and compiled to the same kind of rule

claims.text: Devon makes the same point from the other side: no model provider can write your limits for you.
claims.quote: No model provider can write your limits for you.

claims.text: Sondera's documentation describes an open-source harness that evaluates Cedar policies before an agent's actions run, with the design rule steer, don't block.
claims.quote: evaluates Cedar policies before an agent's actions run

claims.text: Sondera's autoformalization paper, on a medical agent benchmark, formalised more of an 88-rule policy than the 23 rules earlier work had coded by hand.
claims.quote: formalised more of an 88-rule policy than the 23 rules earlier work had coded by hand

claims.text: The site's own policy-as-code work with Open Policy Agent generated code from rows and read it back; Sondera compiles and proves.
claims.quote: we generated code from rows and read it back; they compile and prove.

claims.text: For the article the owner wrote five rules as Cedar and evaluated them with cedarpy 4.12.2: Sondera's example, two session rules, one skill policy row and two business rules.
claims.quote: I wrote five rules as Cedar and evaluated them with cedarpy 4.12.2

claims.text: All fourteen requests evaluated against the five Cedar rules came out as intended.
claims.quote: All fourteen requests came out as intended.

claims.text: The Cedar for the business rules is as short as Sondera's; the hard part is knowing which client is in dispute or which invoice is approved, facts in the CRM and the ledger.
claims.quote: That is a policy question before it is a code question.

claims.text: The AISI paper gives the supply chain figures as 29%, 6% and 0%, where Devon's article has 29.2% and 6.3%; the other figures match.
claims.quote: gives the supply chain figures as 29%, 6% and 0%, where the article has 29.2% and 6.3%

value.unit: per cent, the first supply chain figure

claims.text: Two items could not be confirmed from a primary source: the lawsuit over the Hugging Face incident and the White House quote; neither changes the argument.
claims.quote: Two items I could not confirm from a primary source today

claims.text: Sondera compiles limits into rules and enforces them at the moment of action with proof; the site writes the policy from mechanics to business, measures the hope in it and keeps the evidence in vaults.
claims.quote: Sondera compiles limits into rules and enforces them at the moment of action, with proof.

claims.text: The Cedar was written for this article with cedarpy; it was not run in Sondera's pipeline or harness and not checked with a theorem prover.
claims.quote: The Cedar was written for this article.

claims.text: Where the facts come from is the open part; the business rules assume the session knows what is in dispute and what is approved.
claims.quote: Where the facts come from is the open part.

claims.text: Sondera's benchmark results are theirs and have not been reproduced here.
claims.quote: The benchmark figures are from their paper; I have not reproduced them.

claims.text: Two of Devon's article's items, the lawsuit and the White House quote, are unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Two of the article's items are unconfirmed.

claims.text: No collaboration with Sondera is implied; this is an independent reading of a public article.
claims.quote: This is an independent reading of a public article.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 14 October 2026 after reading Josh Devon's LinkedIn post, written by the site's agent, with a research agent checking the sources.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 14 October 2026, after reading Josh Devon's LinkedIn post
